title: Southwestern Chicken and Black Bean Mason Jar Salad
intro: This desk-friendly salad builds a robust meal for busy weekdays without relying on heavy bottled dressings. The layered approach keeps the greens crisp until you are ready to shake and eat.

ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes
ingredients.canonical_name: Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average

ingredients.name: canned black beans, no-salt-added
ingredients.canonical_name: Beans, black, mature seeds, canned, low sodium

ingredients.name: cooked chicken breast
ingredients.canonical_name: Chicken, broilers or fryers, breast, meat only, cooked, roasted

instructions: Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, cilantro, cumin, and salt in a small bowl to make the dressing.
Divide the dressing into the bottom of large mason jars or tall storage containers.
Layer the halved cherry tomatoes directly into the dressing.
Add the rinsed black beans, thawed corn, and cooked quinoa in even layers on top of the tomatoes.
Place the chopped cooked chicken over the grains and beans.
Pack the chopped romaine lettuce into the top of the jars and secure with lids.
Shake the jars before serving to distribute the dressing over the greens.
variation: Swap the cooked chicken for drained canned low-sodium tuna.
conservation: Keeps 2 to 3 days refrigerated in sealed jars.
validation_warnings: Stage 4 coverage: 'extra-virgin olive oil': [748608] Oil, olive, extra virgin has no USDA value for fiber_g, protein_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [171413] Oil, olive, salad or cooking.

[thirty_minute_practicality] The recipe relies on 'cooked and cooled' quinoa. Cooking and cooling raw quinoa from scratch takes longer than 30 minutes. To honestly meet the book's 30-minute cold-start promise, update the ingredient text to say 'leftover or store-bought pre-cooked pouch quinoa'. It would also be helpful to specify 'cooked chicken breast (such as rotisserie)'.
